desc:
Let k be the number of 1 bits in the binary form of n. Count the integers x with 1 ≤ x ≤ n that also have exactly k bits set.

The range is too large to enumerate, so count combinatorially.

n = 5 -> 2   (3 = 11 and 5 = 101)
n = 8 -> 4   (1, 2, 4 and 8)
n = 7 -> 1   (only 7 itself)
hints: Group the numbers below n by the highest bit position where they differ from n. Such a number has a 0 where n has a 1, and it matches n above that position.
If that position is i, the bits below it are completely free. Only the number of ones among those i bits matters, so it is a binomial coefficient.
Walk the set bits of n from the top. With seen ones above the current bit, add comb(i, k - seen) when that is valid, then add 1 for n itself.
editorial: Let k be the popcount of n. A number x < n is determined by the highest position i where it differs from n; at that position n has a 1 and x has a 0. Above i the two agree, so x already has seen ones, where seen counts the set bits of n above i.

The i lower bits of x are unconstrained, and x needs exactly k - seen ones among them, which gives comb(i, k - seen) choices. Summing this over the set bits of n counts every x < n, and n itself is added at the end. The loop runs over at most 31 bit positions.
